minutes.headline: School Committee held a first read of the revised transportation policy and set a second read for Monday 6:30.
minutes.summary: The committee's only business was the first reading of the transportation policy, using the chair's merged draft built from the policy committee's version and another member's submission. Members edited the wording on wait-list updates and on how seats are assigned for grades 7 to 12, and an edited copy was shared on screen and read again. No vote was needed on a first read; a second read was scheduled for Monday and the final read for the March 15th meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee held a first read of the revised transportation policy; no vote was needed or taken.
The chair's merged draft, built from the policy committee's version and another member's submission, was adopted as the text for the first read.
Members edited the wording on wait-list updates and amended the seat-assignment paragraph to cover grade 7 to 12 applicants on a first come, first served basis.
Members agreed the procedure document stays a draft that administration can change within the policy, rather than being fixed by approving the policy.
A second read was set for Monday at 6:30 pm, with the final read at the March 15th meeting.

why_it_matters: The policy governs how bus seats are assigned, including for grades 7 to 12, so the wording on first come, first served and wait-list updates sets the rules families must follow.
Because the procedure stays a draft that administration can change, the details of how the policy runs may shift without a committee vote.
